hints: Notice the ball momentarily stops at the maximum height of $12.7\text{ m}$, so the downward motion starts from rest with $u = 0$.
With air resistance negligible, acceleration is $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$ downwards, so the fall distance obeys $s = \frac{1}{2}gt_{fall}^2$.
Find $t_{fall}$ from $12.7\text{ m}$, then remember the upward journey to the top takes the same time as the fall back to ground level.
walkthrough: Consider the downward half of the motion only. It starts from rest at $s = 12.7\text{ m}$ above the ground with initial velocity $u = 0$ and acceleration $a = g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$ downwards.
Use $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $u = 0$ to get $s = \frac{1}{2}gt_{fall}^2$, so $t_{fall} = \sqrt{2s/g}$.
This gives $t_{fall} \approx 1.61\text{ s}$ for falling from maximum height to the ground.
Without air resistance the upward motion is symmetric with the downward motion, so time up equals time down.
Total time in the air is $t = 2t_{fall} \approx 2 \times 1.61 = 3.22\text{ s}$. This is option B.
